name: Kbd
summary: Inline keyboard-key cue. A small monospace pill rendered for shortcuts inside Tooltips, DropdownMenu items, help overlays, and onboarding text. Renders mac-or-platform-aware glyphs (⌘ vs Ctrl) when platform='auto'. Use Kbd, not Tag, for keyboard hints — the visual chrome is distinct.

keys.description: The shortcut as space-separated tokens: 'Cmd K', 'Ctrl Shift P', 'Enter'. The component splits on whitespace and renders one Kbd per token, joined by hairline plus signs.

platform.description: auto: detects via navigator.platform / navigator.userAgentData. mac renders ⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ⌃; win/linux render Ctrl Alt Shift.

size.description: xs: 16 px (inside DropdownMenu item right-rail). sm: 20 px (inside Tooltip / inline prose). Don't go larger — Kbd is a cue, not a label.

rules: Render as <kbd> inside the wrapper so SR users hear 'keyboard input'.
Multi-key shortcuts: each key in its own <kbd>, joined by aria-hidden '+' separators.
Glyph translation: mac ⌘/⌥/⇧/⌃ render their character; SR via aria-label on the wrapper announces 'Command K' (not '⌘ K').

do: Use Kbd inside Tooltip / DropdownMenu / onboarding for shortcut cues.
Use the platform symbols on mac (⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ⌃); use spelled-out keys on win/linux (Ctrl Alt Shift).
Pair with a verb: 'Save  ⌘S' — not 'Press ⌘S to save'.
dont: Don't use Kbd for inline code — that's <code> or CodeBlock.
Don't render Kbd larger than sm.
Don't paint Kbd in lime — it's a hint, not an action.

changelog.note: Initial Kbd contract. Platform-aware glyph rendering with SR-friendly key names.
